traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS are implemented and verified:
- **Rule Naming / REQ-RULE-NAME**: The core rule implementation lives in src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts. src/index.ts wires `rules["prefer-supports-annotation"]` as a non-deprecated clone of that rule and marks `rules["prefer-implements-annotation"]` as deprecated with `replacedBy: ["prefer-supports-annotation"]`. plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts confirms both names appear in the exported rules list, and prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts runs the rule under both names. - **Optional Warning / REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING**: The rule’s meta has `type: "suggestion"` and `docs.recommended: false` so it is off by default. processComment reports `preferImplements` for eligible legacy patterns and `cannotAutoFix`/`multiStoryDetected` for non-fixable cases. Tests verify these diagnostics for simple, mixed, and multi-story scenarios. - **Auto-fix Support / REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT**: buildImplementsAutoFix plus applyImplementsReplacement compute a safe fixer only when there is exactly one @story path, one @story line, at least one simple `@req REQ-ID` line, and no @supports in the same comment. The fixer replaces the @story line with a `@supports ...` line and removes the @req lines, preserving the original indentation and `*` prefix. Jest tests assert exact `output` strings for both single and multiple REQ IDs and verify that complex @story/@req lines do not auto-fix but still warn, demonstrating conservative behavior and maintained JSDoc structure. - **Multi-story Detection / REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT**: analyzeComment builds a Set of story paths; hasMultipleStories uses a named threshold constant. processComment emits `multiStoryDetected` when more than one distinct story path exists, and `cannotAutoFix` when mixed with existing @supports. Tests cover both conditions with specific messageIds and reason data. - **Configurable Enforcement / REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY**: The rule is not included in TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES and thus not present in recommended/strict configs. prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts explicitly checks that neither rule key appears in those presets and demonstrates configuration objects using "warn" and "error" severities for both primary and alias keys, satisfying the requirement that teams can choose off/warn/error with default off. - **Both Formats Valid / REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION**: When the rule is disabled (the default), it has no effect; other rules (valid-annotation-format, valid-req-reference, etc.) continue to validate `@story`/`@req` annotations. Within the migration rule itself, valid cases confirm that comments with only @story, only @req, only @supports, or certain mixed forms without both @story and @req are ignored (no diagnostics), ensuring legacy annotations remain valid unless the migration rule is explicitly enabled. - **Valid Output / cross-check with supports rules**: Auto-generated `@supports` lines in tests use correct `.story.md` paths and REQ IDs that conform to the validation patterns used by valid-annotation-format and valid-req-reference. While there is no separate integration test invoking those validators on the fixed code, the generated formats match those validators’ expectations, and the tests’ outputs demonstrate structurally valid `@supports` annotations. - **Documentation**: user-docs/migration-guide.md provides a user-facing migration guide describing `traceability/prefer-supports-annotation`, its deprecated alias, default disabled state, configuration examples, and detailed behavior and auto-fix semantics, including when auto-fix is applied vs. when only diagnostics are emitted.
All related Jest tests pass in the latest run, confirming the behavior is implemented and stable. Therefore this story is fully implemented and marked PASSED.
